chunks: Ali, from the one who narrated it to him, said:

A son was born to me, so I wrote seeking permission regarding his purification on the seventh day. The reply came: “Do not do it.” Then he died on the seventh day or the eighth. Then I wrote informing of his death, and the reply came: “You will be granted another in his place and another besides him. You shall name him Ahmad, and after Ahmad, Ja‘far.” So it came to pass just as he had said.

He said: I prepared for hajj and bade the people farewell, and I was about to depart, when the reply came: “We are averse to that, though the matter is up to you.” He said: My chest became constricted and I became grieved, so I wrote: “I remain committed to hearing and obedience, except that I am grieved by my staying back from hajj.” Then the signed reply came: “Let not your chest be constricted, for you will perform hajj next year, if Allah wills.” He said:

And when the following year came, I wrote seeking permission, and permission was granted. Then I wrote: “I have taken Muḥammad ibn al-‘Abbās as my travel companion, and I am confident in his religiosity and trustworthiness.” The reply came: “Al-Asadī is an excellent travel companion, so if he comes, do not prefer anyone over him.” Then al-Asadī came, and I took him as my travel companion.
ai.seo_question: How does this hadith describe the Imam’s guidance about family matters and hajj?
ai.summary: This hadith narrates fulfilled reports conveyed by the Imam عليه السلام concerning the death of a child, the later birth and naming of children, and the postponement and later completion of hajj. It also records the narrator’s obedience to the Imam’s guidance and the Imam’s direction regarding a suitable travel companion.
